newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister sees 97/98 wheat output 17-18 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister sees 97/98 wheat output 17-18 mln T.

text.p: Turkey's Agriculture Minister Musa Demirci said on Thursday the country's 1997/98 wheat production would almost be the same as last year's output of 17 to 18 million tonnes.

He told a news conference that the state grain board (TMO) was planning to buy 3.7 million tonnes of grain from farmers in 1997/98, 2.5 million tonnes of that being wheat which compares to 650,000 tonnes of wheat purchased by the TMO a year earlier.
"We have had an effective struggle with bug diseases and we are hoping that this year's wheat crop will be around the same levels of last year which was 17-18 million tonnes," he said.

"The TMO has made itself ready for the financing of the grain purchases. It will make cash payments for the purchases," he told the conference where he announced grain base prices for the 1997/98 crop year.
The TMO's planned purchases for 1997/98 roughly amount to $750 million, according to the base prices, which Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller briefly announced on Wednesday night.
According to the announcement, the government offers 33,000 lira per kg ($235.7 per tonne) of hard red wheat in June, up 83.3 percent from last year's initial price.
The price will be increased by 2,000 lira every month to keep up with the inflation rate, Demirci said.
Immediate comments from farmer groups suggest that Turkish grain growers were satisfied with the base prices for this year.
"We have welcome the government's base prices for wheat and other grains," said the Union of Agricultural Chambers (TZOB) in a statement.
"We are very pleased with the prices announced higher than the world grain prices," it said.
Demirci said the TMO would buy a total of 3.7 million tonnes of grain, compared to more than 1.5 million tonnes bought last year.
"I think whole purchases will total 100-110 trillion lira this year," he said.
